correctness.rationale: For fixed \(0<R<1\), the finite SIR epidemic is coupled to the finite-moment, subcritical multitype birth–death genealogy by rejecting transmissions to previously infected uniformly chosen targets. Dominated convergence of the cumulative collision functional gives \(J_M\to J_\infty\). The exact census relation is \((1-R)\mathbb E T_M=1-RJ_M/M\). Generator equations for first moments, active-pair second moments and active–cumulative moments integrate to \(\bar Y=[n(1-R)]^{-1}(I-RP)^{-1}\) and \(\bar X=[n(1-R)]^{-1}(I-RP)^{-2}\). These imply the claimed trace correction and its \(o(M^{-1})\) remainder, while the Neumann series yields positivity. Along the interpolation \(P_\theta=\theta I+(1-\theta)Q\), each eigenvalue increases or stays fixed and at least one increases; the scalar derivative \(f_R'(x)=(1+Rx)/(1-Rx)^3\) is strictly positive on \([-1,1]\). Exact-rational package checks independently verify finite-SIR recursions and integrated moment identities, including the three rational two-patch coefficients. No extension to critical or growing-dimensional settings is asserted.

value.rationale: The motivating model identifies mean outbreak size and spatial architecture as epidemiologically substantive observables and relies on branching approximations at large population size. This theorem quantifies the first systematic failure of the topology-blind subcritical branching prediction: a mathematically natural closed-walk return statistic. Its sharp universal strict response to within-patch mixing reveals a principled topology effect while total reproduction number and leading mean are unchanged, and it identifies an exact computable correction usable to compare different network structures. It is not a mere random numerical slice or a restatement of a general matrix identity; the exact probabilistic coefficient must be proved by the coupled SIR–branching collision calculation.
